name: Passing Directness
desc: Average pass length.
pro: Short: keeps the ball and tires the opponent. Direct: gets forward fast and ignores the press.
con: Short demands Passing/Technique/Composure from everyone. Direct loses more balls without a target/pace up front.

name: Tempo
desc: Speed of decision-making on the ball.
pro: High: catches the opponent disorganised. Low: control and patience.
con: High + short passing demands high Decisions/Technique; more tiring.

name: Attacking Width
desc: How wide the team is in possession.
pro: Wide: stretches the opponent’s block and opens inside channels. Narrow: central combinations.
con: Wide makes reacting to a turnover harder (counter-press). Narrow makes it easier for the opponent to close the middle.

name: Creative Freedom
desc: Freedom to deviate from the plan.
pro: Expressive: top players find solutions. Disciplined: predictable, safe execution.
con: Expressive with players weak in Decisions/Flair = chaos.

name: Attacking Transition
desc: What to do after winning the ball.
pro: Counter: exploits a disorganised defence. Hold Shape: resets and takes control of possession.
con: Counter without pace/outlets leads to quick turnovers.

name: Play for Set Pieces
desc: Try to win, or avoid winning, corners and free kicks (new in FM27).
pro: Play for Set Pieces pays off with good headers and set-piece takers.
con: Keep Ball in Play keeps the tempo but wastes a weapon if you are strong in the air.

name: Time Wasting
desc: Managing the clock.
pro: Useful when winning late on.
con: Can irritate opponents/the referee; breaks your own team’s rhythm.

name: Pass Reception
desc: Pass into space or to feet (new in FM26).
pro: To feet: control. Into space: depth and speed.
con: To feet against a high press demands First Touch/Composure. Into space demands Off the Ball/Acceleration.

name: Build-up Strategy
desc: Play out short through the press or bypass it (new in FM26).
pro: Through: draws in and breaks the press. Bypass: minimum risk at the back.
con: Through with technically weak GK/centre-backs = goals conceded. Bypass loses possession.

name: Goal Kicks
desc: Type of goal kick.
pro: Short: starts the build-up. Long: skips the press to the target.
con: Short against a high press with defenders weak on the ball is risky.

name: GK Distribution Speed
desc: Goalkeeper distribution speed.
pro: Quick feeds counter-attacks.
con: Quick with the team out of position loses the ball.

name: GK Distribution
desc: Where the goalkeeper distributes.
pro: Direct the ball to your strength (a technical centre-back, a quick wing-back, a tall striker).
con: Predictable: the opponent can set a trap.

name: Supporting Runs
desc: Full-backs/wing-backs support inside (underlap) or outside (overlap).
pro: Overlap with inside wingers; underlap with wide wingers.
con: It clashes with the role: a W with overlaps crowds the channel.

name: Dribbling
desc: How often players carry/dribble the ball.
pro: Encourage with quality dribblers.
con: Encouraging with poor Dribbling = turnovers in dangerous areas.

name: Progress Through
desc: Preferred zone for progressing the ball.
pro: Focus on the side of your best player or the opponent’s weak spot.
con: Predictable; the opponent can overload that side.

name: Final Third Patience
desc: Deliver early crosses into the box or patiently work the ball into shooting positions.
pro: Work Ball Into Box: higher-quality chances. Hit Early Crosses: catches the defence before it sets.
con: Work Ball Into Box against a low block can produce sterile possession; Hit Early Crosses wastes possession without good targets.

name: Shots from Distance
desc: How often players shoot from outside the box.
pro: Encourage with good shooters against low blocks.
con: Poor shots waste possession.

name: Crossing Style
desc: Type of cross.
pro: Low for quick strikers; Floated for aerial targets.
con: Floated without players strong in the air is a waste.

name: Line of Engagement
desc: Where the team starts pressing.
pro: High: wins the ball near the opponent’s goal. Low: compact block, invites them out.
con: High demands Stamina/Work Rate; disconnected from the defensive line it opens space between the lines.

name: Defensive Line
desc: Height of the defensive line.
pro: High: compact team, opponent far from goal. Low: protects the space in behind.
con: High needs quick centre-backs and a Sweeper Keeper. Low invites pressure and shots.

name: Trigger Press
desc: How often players trigger the press.
pro: More: high recoveries, chaos for the opponent.
con: Physically draining; uncoordinated pressing is easily beaten.

name: Defensive Transition
desc: Immediate reaction to losing the ball.
pro: Counter-Press: wins the ball back before the opponent organises. Regroup: protects the shape.
con: Counter-Press with a very open/tired team gets played through in transition.

name: Tackling
desc: Aggression in the tackle.
pro: Get Stuck In wins more duels.
con: More fouls and cards; dangerous with defenders who have low Tackling.

name: Pressing Trap
desc: Where the ball carrier is forced (mid block/high press).
pro: Outside: corners them on the flank. Inside: forces them into a crowded middle.
con: Outside without aggressive full-backs/wingers does not close the trap; Inside needs a strong midfield.

name: Cross Engagement
desc: Allow or stop crosses (low block).
pro: Invite: with centre-backs dominant in the air. Stop: with short defenders.
con: Invite without centre-backs strong in the air = headed goals.

name: Short Goalkeeper Distribution
desc: Press the opposing keeper’s short distribution (High Press section).
pro: Yes forces the opponent to go long.
con: It means pushing strikers and midfielders up — more space in behind.

name: Defensive Line Behaviour
desc: Whether the line drops to protect depth or steps up to squeeze space (new in FM27).
pro: Step Up: compact team, catches players offside. Drop Off: protects the space in behind.
con: Step Up with slow centre-backs is dangerous; Drop Off separates the defence from midfield.
